text:
Zoe Bennett: Hi all, accepted my GitHub org invite but it attached to my personal account (zoe.dev) and now the repo list shows 'Request access' for the team repos. I didn't add my work email to my personal account. Any way to fix without touching my personal account? :confused:

people-ops: Welcome Zoe! Yes we can remediate. Short options: 1) We revoke the old invite and reissue to your work email (zoe@redwood.com) and enforce SSO mapping; or 2) you can add your work email to your personal account temporarily then accept and we'll remap. If you prefer not to touch personal, choose option 1 and accept on desktop.

Zoe Bennett: I'd prefer option 1. Reissue please. Also FYI the GitHub mobile app finished my SSO on my phone and I think that may have linked the wrong account earlier.

infra-bot: Note: mobile app flows can cause the wrong account to approve SSO if multiple accounts are logged in. Best to accept org invites on desktop to avoid that interception.

Carlos Medina: Re-sent the invite to zoe@redwood.com and flagged it for enforced SSO. Zoe, accept in a desktop browser and when prompted click 'Authorize SSO' — then sign out/in to flush sessions. If you still see 'Request access' ping here.

Zoe Bennett: Accepted the new invite, completed SSO, but when I try to clone a repo via SSH I get "Permission denied (publickey)" and HTTPS push gives 403. I have an old SSH key loaded for my personal account. :grimacing:

people-ops: Two things to try: 1) add a new work SSH key (ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "zoe@redwood.com") and add the pubkey to GitHub Settings -> SSH and GPG keys; or 2) clear OS credential helper entries so HTTPS pushes use work credentials. Which OS are you on?

Zoe Bennett: macOS. I created a new key and added it, but `ssh -T git@github.com` still connects as my personal user. The agent is offering the old key first.

Carlos Medina: On mac you can list identities with `ssh-add -l` and remove the personal one `ssh-add -d ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_personal`. Then add the work key `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work`. Also make sure your ~/.ssh/config has a Host entry for github.com specifying the correct IdentityFile for the repo: 

```
Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```

That forces the work key.

Zoe Bennett: Did that and `ssh -T` now shows "Hi zoe! You've successfully authenticated" but the username shown is still zoe.dev. However I can now clone and push. Why does the auth name show the personal handle?

people-ops: The greeting usually reflects the account associated with the key. If the public key you added to GitHub is mapped to your work account, the greeting should show your work username. Double-check which account the pubkey is attached to under GitHub -> Settings -> SSH and GPG keys. If the key was accidentally added to the personal account, remove it there and add to the work account.

Zoe Bennett: Ah — I accidentally uploaded the pubkey to my personal account before logging out. Removed it and added to the work account. `ssh -T` now greets my work handle. Repos and pushes behave normally now. Thanks! :tada:

Carlos Medina: Great. Final checklist we recommend for anyone in this flow: 1) Accept invites on desktop, 2) ensure the invite email matches the account you accept with, 3) complete SSO, sign out/in, 4) clear OS credential helper or use `gh auth login`, 5) add work SSH key and ensure agent/ssh_config points to it. We'll add this checklist to the onboarding message.

people-ops: Nice troubleshooting, Zoe. If anyone else hits cross-account issues, DM people-ops with your GitHub username and the invite email and we'll handle the reissue. Welcome to Redwood! :wave:
